body:
**Correcting my own recommendation above: wiring `lint.yml` is worth doing now, and I had this backwards.**

I said it would be a no-op gate. It is not. `eslint.config.js` already carries **three `error`-level rules whose stated purpose is to fail CI** — and because `lint.yml` only runs on `workflow_dispatch`, **all three have never gated anything.**

```js
// ADR-0054 Phase 5 ratchet — ban synthetic-event triggers (C1). Error so a
// new violation fails CI; the existing surfaces were converted to direct
// idempotent commands first, so this lints clean today.
'object-ui/no-synthetic-event-trigger': 'error',

// objectui#2879 ratchet — a hook called inside try/catch desyncs hook order
// when the catch swallows a throw. ... Error so a tenth copy fails CI; all
// known sites were converted first, so this lints clean today.
'object-ui/no-try-catch-around-hook': 'error',

// ... Error so a new inline mirror fails CI; the covered fields were
// converted first, so this lints clean today.
'object-ui/no-inline-spec-config': 'error',   // scoped to packages/types/src/objectql.ts
```

Three separate deliberate efforts — ADR-0054 Phase 5, #2879, and the `objectql.ts` type-discipline ratchet — each written on the assumption that CI enforces it. Each author even pre-cleaned the violations so the rule would "lint clean today." **The enforcement they were built against does not exist.** That is the same shape as #2911, one layer up: the rule is authored, the runtime never runs it.

And the cost of switching it on is **zero**: `pnpm lint` reports **0 errors** across all 38 packages today, precisely because those sites were pre-cleaned. Wiring the workflow activates three intended ratchets immediately with no cleanup.

So the corrected recommendation is **wire `lint.yml` on PRs now** — not for the reason I originally gave (it still would *not* have caught #2911; see below), but because three ratchets are currently inert.

## What wiring it does and does not buy

**Does:** activates the three `object-ui/*` ratchets, so a new synthetic-event trigger, a new hook-in-try/catch, or a new inline spec mirror fails a PR — as their authors intended.

**Does not:** catch #2911. `no-unused-vars` is `'warn'`, and warnings never fail without `--max-warnings`. That part of my original analysis stands.

## Actual composition of the 7,724 warnings

Now measured properly rather than sampled:

| rule | count | share |
|---|---:|---:|
| `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` | **6,262** | 81% |
| `react-refresh/only-export-components` | 486 | 6% |
| `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` | **322** | 4% |
| `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` | 252 | 3% |
| `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` | 177 | 2% |
| `react-hooks/refs` | 111 | 1% |
| `react-hooks/use-memo` | 33 | |
| `react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization` | 32 | |
| `react-hooks/immutability` | 12 | |
| `react-hooks/incompatible-library` | 2 | |

**One rule is 81% of the noise.** That reframes option 2 above: a `--max-warnings` baseline of 7,724 is really "6,262 `any`s plus 1,462 of everything else," and `no-explicit-any` is a style/discipline call on a codebase whose adapters legitimately use `any`. Ratcheting the aggregate mostly ratchets that one rule.

Note also that five of the `react-hooks/*` rules are explicitly downgraded with the comment *"Downgrade new React Compiler rules to warnings (codebase predates these rules)"* — a deliberate choice, not neglect. Those ~440 should stay warnings.

All 322 `no-unused-vars` are the `'X' is defined but never used` / `is assigned a value but never used` form — i.e. exactly the #2911 class.

## Revised plan

1. **Wire `lint.yml` to `pull_request` / `push` as-is.** Free, no cleanup, activates three dead ratchets. Do this first and separately — it is a pure win and easy to review.
2. **Then, optionally, promote `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` to `error`** after clearing its 322 violations. `argsIgnorePattern: '^_'` is already configured, so unused params just need `_` prefixes; unused imports/locals are mostly deletions. This is the piece that would have caught #2911.
3. **Leave `no-explicit-any` and the React Compiler rules at `warn`.** 6,262 + ~440, both deliberate. Do not put them behind `--max-warnings` without a separate decision.

Do **not** add `--max-warnings=7724` as a blanket cap — it reads as a health signal while being dominated by one stylistic rule.
